# Figures (generated by figures/index.py; do not edit)

Run profile: **full** (5,000 Monte Carlo draws; formats png at 600 dpi). Every figure is drawn by the figures/ package from the data files listed (compute / draw separation).

Manuscript numbering:

Repository numbers = manuscript numbers; the renumbering of each version is in data/ed_number_map.csv, data/sf_number_map.csv and data/st_number_map.csv.

## Main paper (paper_main/)

### Fig1_floor_area

**Fig1 Floor area: history and projection by demand band** — Floor area built per year by demand band: history as census-interval means (columns), the Reference projection annually from 2026 (2026 observed). Positive bands stacked up from zero, negative bands (the starting surplus and the overbuild absorbed, unconsented additions) down from zero. The black line is the floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (history from consents, projection from 2026); the grey caps on the history columns are the census-interval means. 2026 overbuild: observed 2026 building above need, fading from 2027; it is absorbed by 2035 together with the starting surplus (the 2024-25 building beyond the stock identity, carried into 2026). Building runs below need in 2028-2035 while the 2024-27 surplus is absorbed (absorption by 2030 or 2045 changes cumulative carbon by −0.2%/+0.3%, Extended Data Fig. 8).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig1_floor_area.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/bands_history.csv`, `data/baseline/bands_annual.csv`, `data/baseline/annual.csv`, `data/baseline/overbuild_2026.json`
- This run: Completions = 0.945 x consents lagged 17 months (median consent-to-completion time 1.27-1.53 yr; Greenaway-McGrevy & Jones 2023; Jones, Greenaway-McGrevy & Crow 2025; consistent with the Stats NZ Experimental building indicators). Households after the 2023 census = ERP / household-size path (Stats NZ DHE not used). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: building observed (consents to September 2026); the part above modelled need fades from 2028 (ρ = 0.43) and is absorbed by 2035. 2026 population: Stats NZ ERP nowcast. Six display bands (data/bands_display_map.csv); market balance = unexplained building + retirement villages (out of scope) + overbuild / pipeline excess + surplus absorbed (the starting surplus and the overbuild) + surplus kept vacant. Negative bands drawn down from zero: Market balance, Smaller households, Vacancy, Net replacement. Black line: floor area built (in scope), annual 1992-2050 (straight segments between year centres; history 1992-2025 from consents, projection from 2026); grey caps: census-interval means of the history columns (the mean of the annual values over each interval, checked). 2026-2050: 105.4 Mm².

### Fig3_reference_boundaries

**Fig3 The Reference against the planetary boundaries** — (a) Annual carbon, Monte Carlo median with 50% and 90% bands, against the acquired-rights (AR) and ability-to-pay (AtP) boundaries and their zones; (b) cumulative carbon 2026-2050 with its Monte Carlo 90% interval (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon) and 50% interval (25th-75th), the AR and AtP budgets, and the committed emissions after 2050: C1-C4 and B2/B4 after 2050, each a range (lower = 2050 factors held, the carbon-bearing materials of C1-C4 at 2025 in both bounds; upper = 2025 factors), drawn at the lower bound. Building runs below need in 2028-2035 while the 2024-27 surplus is absorbed (absorption by 2030 or 2045 changes cumulative carbon by −0.2%/+0.3%, Extended Data Fig. 8).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig3_reference_boundaries.png`
- Data: `data/aesa/annual.csv`, `data/montecarlo/annual_REF.csv`, `data/montecarlo/draws_REF.csv`, `data/baseline/projection.json`
- This run: Cumulative 2026-2050 25,503 kt (LoE AR 5.76, AtP 22.9); Monte Carlo 90% interval 21,197-30,569 kt (5th-95th percentile of the cumulative carbon of the draws), 50% interval 23,649-27,459 kt, median 25,521 kt (capped bars, no median mark; the column is the deterministic Reference); committed after 2050 (drawn at the lower bound): C1-C4 5,529 kt (5,702 kt with 2025 factors; the carbon-bearing materials, 86% of it, held at 2025 in both bounds, the energy part at the 2050 generic factor in the lower) and B2/B4 after 2050 4,026 kt (2050 factors held; 4,960 kt with 2025 factors); Monte Carlo median 9,553 kt, 50% interval 8,907-10,269, 90% interval 8,014-11,314 kt. Committed range from the Monte Carlo floor-area uncertainty (population, household size, dwelling size, completion rate); repair and end-of-life factors held at their central values. Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and TL: deterministic runs. Lines are shape-preserving (PCHIP) interpolation through the annual values, not smoothed across the observed -> modelled join after 2027; bands: Monte Carlo 90% band pchip, Monte Carlo 50% band pchip.

### Fig4_pathways

**Fig4 The Pathways: the sequential waterfalls** — Sequential waterfalls of cumulative carbon 2026-2050 from the Reference, levers added in PAS 2080 order: (a) L1 ... L10 at Moderate -> Moderate Pathway; (b) at Ambitious -> Ambitious Pathway; (c) L1 at TL ... L10 at TL cumulative -> Theoretical Limit. Each step is one bar coloured by strategy with its net change; AR (solid) and AtP (dotted) budgets with their zones; order-free Shapley values in Fig6.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig4_pathways.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall.csv`, `data/pathways/waterfall_tl_from_reference.csv`
- This run: Cumulative LoE AR: REF 5.76, pathway-moderate 3.89, pathway-ambitious 2.59, TL 0.94. (a-c) Reference 25,503 kt -> Moderate Pathway 17,209 kt, Ambitious Pathway 11,471 kt, Theoretical Limit 4,177 kt; budgets AR 4,427 kt, AtP 1,113 kt. Steps in PAS 2080 order; each step is credited with what remains after the higher-priority measures; order-free Shapley values in Fig6. Net-positive steps: none.

### Fig5_solution_space

**Fig5 The solution space** — Cumulative level of exceedance of AR over uniform cuts of 2027-2050 floor area (x) and of carbon per m2 (y) (after Horup et al. 2025), with S1-S3 (Moderate filled, Ambitious hollow), the Moderate / Ambitious Pathway and the Theoretical Limit; analytic LoE AR contours and the exact AR line. Right: the cumulative LoE AR ruler (log) with the Reference, the Pathways, TL, AR = 1 and AtP; the same marker size per run in the plane, the ruler and the legend.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig5_solution_space.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/solution_space.csv`, `data/pathways/backcast.json`, `data/pathways/runs.csv`
- This run: LoE AR = [1,207 + 24,296 (1 - x)(1 - y)] / 4,427 kt; C_2026 = the 2026 cohort's emissions in the window; plane floor C_2026 / B_AR = 0.273 (the lowest LoE AR at x or y = 100%); AtP = B_AtP / B_AR = 0.251 lies below the floor, so the AtP contour is outside the plotted square (y = 100.4% at x = 0). Axes -5% to 90%.

### Fig6_shapley_levers

**Fig6 What each lever removes** — Shapley values within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; exact, 1,024 subsets) on cumulative carbon 2026-2050: rows grouped by PAS 2080 strategy (S1 Avoid, S2 Switch, S3 Improve: L9 construction-stage carbon and L10 production decarbonisation) in the lever order and coloured by strategy; filled bar Moderate, hollow bar Ambitious, large dot TL. The TL dots are Shapley values within the TL game (all ten levers at their limit), so they include each lever's interactions at the limit; L5 (occupancy density) interacts with L4 (extra space): both act on the floor area per dwelling.

- Files: `paper_main/Fig6_shapley_levers.png`
- Data: `data/pathways/shapley.csv`
- This run: (a) Standalone: each lever alone vs the Reference (not additive). (b) Shapley shares within each combined game (Reference -> Moderate Pathway, -> Ambitious Pathway, -> TL; 1,024 subsets per game); the TL shares include interactions at the limit (L5 with L4). Game totals (= Reference - Pathway / TL): moderate 8,294 kt, ambitious 14,032 kt, tl 21,326 kt.

### Fig7_uncertainty

**Fig7 Uncertainty** — (a) One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative LoE AR 2026-2050, each input at its low and high end per its definition (population rows move the budgets with the path; AR base-window rows move the AR budget only); rows are shown from the completion-rate range up, without the completion-rate and no-2026-data rows (both in Extended Data Fig. 8; the rows with a smaller range are named, with their ranges, in the note); not additive, not a joint interval. (b) The Reference, the Moderate and Ambitious Pathways and the Theoretical Limit: cumulative LoE AR against the 2050 New Zealand population on the same paired Monte Carlo draws, P(LoE AR <= 1) of each with its Wilson 95% interval, LoE = 1, and the population at which the Theoretical Limit has P(LoE AR <= 1) = 50% (Firth logistic; bootstrap 95% CI).

- Files: `paper_main/Fig7_uncertainty.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/tornado.csv`, `data/sensitivity/planetary_boundary.csv`, `data/pathways/montecarlo_draws.csv`, `data/pathways/annual.csv`, `data/pathways/montecarlo_conditional_tl.json`, `data/baseline/scenarios.json`, `data/aesa/results.json`
- This run: (b) Below about 6.2 M (every draw below 6.03 M; 257 draws in all) the Theoretical Limit LoE AR flattens at about 0.6 (median 0.60, range 0.58–0.64): the dwellings released by L1 at TL (household merging) and L2 at TL (the vacancy fall to 1.31%) plus the starting surplus cover all positive need after the pipeline, so TL builds no new dwellings after 2027 and its carbon is that of the observed 2026–27 pipeline (9.48 Mm²), which does not fall with population (correlation 0.01 over these draws; a year with negative need builds nothing and nothing is demolished). (a) Reference LoE AR 5.761; population rows move the budgets with the path; the AR base-window row moves the AR budget only; one-at-a-time ranges are not additive. Rows in Extended Data Fig. 8 only: Completion rate (0.93–0.96); No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025). The carbon-factor rows (Carbon factors (jackknife), LoE AR 5.734–5.771 against carbon −3.4% / +3.2%) are not shown: their LoE range falls below the row filter (the range of the completion-rate row) because the AR base co-varies with the factors, so the AR budget moves with the carbon. (b) P(TL within AR) = 0.609 (Wilson 0.596-0.623; n = 5,000); P(LoE AR <= 1) on the same paired draws: Reference 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Moderate Pathway 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Ambitious Pathway 0.0000 (Wilson 0.0000-0.0008), Theoretical Limit 0.6092 (Wilson 0.5956-0.6226); threshold 6.693 M (95% CI 6.690-6.695 M; Firth penalised likelihood (MLE does not exist), 2000 resamples).

### ED4_stock_vacancy

**ED4 Vacancy and dwellings per year by component** — (a) Vacancy rate of empty private dwellings: census values (filled; open where the 2013 split is estimated), the series on one consistent definition, the rate held at its 2023 value in the projection, and the implied rate including the surplus still to be absorbed. (b) Dwellings per year by component: census intervals as interval means (columns), the pipeline years 2026-2027 as annual columns and the projection as stacked areas; positive components are stacked up and negative ones down from zero, and the line is the dwellings built in scope. The row at the top gives the market balance of each census interval (thousand dwellings per year). 1986-1991 is not covered (the calibration starts in 1991). In the last column (after the 2023 Census) households are population divided by the household size of the model, not census-benchmarked.

- Files: `paper_extended/ED4_stock_vacancy.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D05_stock_and_vacancy.json`, `data/baseline/scenarios.json`, `data/baseline/projection.json`
- This run: a: Census range, one definition = the census 1986–2023 range on one definition; Definition break = the 2013 → 2018 empty / away definition break; History (census empty) = the Reference history, census empty / private dwellings (before 2013: unoccupied × the 2013 empty share), linear between censuses; One definition (sensitivity) = one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, not used by the Reference; Held at 2023 = the Reference projection held at the 2023 census value; Implied = implied by the held rate + the unabsorbed starting surplus and 2026 overbuild / stock; Census empty, 2013 split = the 2013 split applied; All unoccupied (rejected) = empty + residents away. The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild raise implied stock vacancy temporarily and are absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). b: History: one column per census interval (interval means; vacancy on one definition, the pooled 2018/2023 empty share, 49.2% of unoccupied dwellings); between censuses annual detail is not identified; 1986-91 is not covered (the calibration starts in 1991). The 2024–2025 column: households are population / household size (model), not census-benchmarked; its market balance (9,020 dwellings a year) is the F1 residual, carried into 2026 as the starting surplus (18,966 dwellings). Pipeline years 2026, 2027: annual columns; projection from 2028: annual stacked areas. In the pipeline years the line is the sum of the components (the stock-identity count: observed building less the modelled retirement-village share); the in-scope floor area divided by the dwelling size held at its 2023–2025 mean gives 2026: 30,045 (−51); 2027: 35,540 (−801) (the pipeline floor area is observed, the dwelling size held). History: net replacement is census-measured, the rate of the census dwelling-count identity of each interval (ED5; under-construction corrected) x the previous year's stock, the quantity the model uses (2024–2025: the latest rate carried). Top row: the market balance per census interval (thousand dwellings per year). Market balance: building above (+) or below (−) what household growth, vacancy and net replacement require. History: the residual of the census stock identity (includes measurement error). 2024–25: carried into 2026 as starting surplus (18,966 vacant dwellings: the residual above the census-interval mean x 2 years). 2026–27: the observed pipeline above need. From 2028: the surplus absorbed by 2035. The same band as Fig1's market balance (checked in 32 intervals and years: the same sign everywhere, and Fig1 = the dwellings x the in-scope floor area per dwelling after the pipeline; Fig1 also counts the retirement villages, drawn here on their own). Projection: net replacement, retirement villages (negative) and the market balance. Net replacement = demolition − unconsented additions (+ the recent surge in the Reference); the census measures only the net. The projection's split (demolition at the BRANZ rate, 0.135%/yr; the calibrated residual as unconsented additions, −0.076%/yr; the surge) is not identified from data and is not drawn. Positive parts are stacked up from zero and negative parts down from zero, all solid (no outlines, hatching or fades); up + down = the net of every column and year (checked). The line is the annual dwellings built (in scope), straight between annual values; the grey caps are its census-interval means (equal to the column nets, checked). The row at the top: the market balance of each census interval (thousand dwellings per year).

### ED7_boundary_sensitivity

**ED7 Boundary definitions and allocation: cumulative LoE of AR and of AtP** — One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative level of exceedance 2026-2050 of (a) acquired rights (AR) and (b) ability to pay (AtP): boundary definitions (carrying capacity, global impact, AR base window), allocation, population, replacement, the summation window (2028-2050 only: carbon and budget both summed over 2028-2050, the pipeline years excluded; the AR base unchanged) and whole-life accounting (committed emissions after 2050 counted at construction, the AR base recomputed on the same convention). Each input is shown at its low (pale blue) and high (dark blue) end, a single alternative case in grey; the ranges are not additive. Not shown (kept in the data file): α = 1 (Hjalsted et al. SI tables) and the raw Stats NZ 2024-base median population. What each row changes compared with the Reference: Carrying capacity: 1 W/m² boundary (not 2 °C): 1 W/m² planetary boundary (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), safe operating space 3.61 × 10¹² kg CO₂e per year, instead of the 2 °C carrying capacity (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015), 6.81 × 10¹² (the same global impact); both budgets move. Global impact: EF 3.1: global impact (I_glob) from the EF 3.1 normalisation factor (Andreasi Bassi et al. 2023, Table 10; 7.55 × 10³ kg CO₂e per person, 2010) instead of 5.58 × 10¹³ (Bjørn & Hauschild 2015; equal to the EF 3.0 factor, 8.10 × 10³ per person). The 6.7% difference is mainly the lower characterisation factor of methane in EF 3.1. Acquired rights only. AR base window (5–34 yr): mean sector emissions over 5 / 20 / 34 years (2021–2025, 2006–2025, 1992–2025) instead of 10 years (2016–2025); AR only. Economic allocation measure: GDP per capita, current US$: GDP per capita in current US$ instead of GDP per capita at purchasing-power parity, constant 2021 international $ (World Bank WDI); AtP only. Sector share: ratio of sums (not mean of ratios): FCE share of GDP in the sector share: the ratio of the summed FCE to the summed GDP of the 40 quarters 2016–2025 instead of the mean of the 40 quarterly FCE/GDP ratios 2016–2025; AtP only. Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median; carbon and both budgets move together. Population source: UN WPP 2024 median: UN WPP 2024 median for New Zealand instead of the model's population path (the Stats NZ 2024-base median from the observed 2025 level, with the observed 2026 growth); budgets only. Replacement (Low–Very High): as in Extended Data Fig. 8 (carbon only; the budgets are unchanged). Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): as in Extended Data Fig. 8 (carbon only). 2028–2050 only (pipeline years excluded): carbon and both budgets summed over 2028–2050 instead of 2026–2050 (the observed pipeline years excluded); the AR base unchanged. Whole-life accounting (committed at construction): every life-cycle stage, including the emissions committed after 2050, counted in the construction year; the AR base recomputed on the same convention.

### ED8_one_at_a_time

**ED8 One at a time: cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050 of the Reference and of the Theoretical Limit** — (a) One-at-a-time ranges of the Reference cumulative embodied carbon 2026-2050, grouped by category; each input at its low (pale blue) and high (dark blue) end, a single alternative case grey, intermediate cases as ticks; the ranges are not additive and are not a joint interval. Not shown (kept in the data file): the overbuild gap against the same-year requirement, no census under-construction correction, the maintenance event timing L / n, and the rows that compare with superseded settings. (b) The Theoretical Limit under two L10 sensitivities, every other lever at TL, against the central Theoretical Limit (vertical line): the near-zero factor of cement (125/850) on every material class without a documented near-zero definition, steel keeping its own (an upper bound on L10, not a documented scenario: no documented near-zero definition exists outside steel and cement), and the near-zero share of cement and steel production 100% by 2050 instead of 93%; values and P(cumulative LoE of AR ≤ 1) over the Monte Carlo draws in Supplementary Table 13. What each row of (a) changes compared with the Reference: Living arrangements: propensities change (Stats NZ B): Stats NZ Medium B household projection (living-arrangement propensities change, modelled on the 2001–2023 censuses) instead of Medium A (propensities held at 2023): what if B happens anyway (the same path is L1 Ambitious, what if policy delivers it). Population (5th–95th pct.): Stats NZ 2024-base stochastic projection, 5th / 95th percentile path instead of the median, with the household size of the Stats NZ Low / High A household projection (the same percentiles). Household size (2018–23 pace): household size continues linearly from 2023 at the 2018–2023 census-interval pace instead of the Stats NZ household-size path rebased on 2023. After 2048: held flat (zero slope): a zero slope imposed at 2048 and household size held constant after it instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. After 2048: PCHIP end slope: the shape-preserving (PCHIP) end derivative at 2048, continued linearly, instead of the 2043–2048 secant slope at 2048, continued linearly in 2049–2050. Dwelling-size reference window 2016–2025: new-dwelling size held at its 2016–2025 mean per typology instead of the 2023–2025 mean. No starting surplus (2024–25 excess not carried): no starting surplus instead of 18,966 vacant dwellings at the start of 2026, absorbed by 2035: (the 2024–2025 building beyond the stock identity, 9,020 dwellings a year, minus the 1992–2023 census-interval mean, −463) × 2 years; carried because it exceeds the mean + 2 SD (SD 3,038). 2026 overbuild booked as stock-neutral redevelopment: the 2026 overbuild (building above need in 2026–2027 and its continuation, fading at ρ = 0.43) replaces existing dwellings instead of adding to the stock: no surplus, so no absorption payback and no soil carbon loss on it. Completion rate (0.93–0.96): 0.93 / 0.96 of consented dwellings completed instead of 0.945. Starting surplus minus 2 SD: a starting surplus of 6,812 dwellings (only the excess above the mean + 2 SD) instead of 18,966. Vacancy rate: 1986–2023 census mean: the mean of the 1986–2023 censuses on one definition instead of the 2023 census value (5.39%). Surplus absorbed (by 2030–by 2045): the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild absorbed by 2030 / 2045 instead of 2035. Completion lag (15–19 months): consents lagged 15 / 19 months instead of 17. No 2026 data (consents to Dec 2025): consents to December 2025 and the projected 2026 population instead of consents to September 2026 and the observed 2026 population growth. Replacement (Low–Very High): Low: the 1991–2023 long-run net rate throughout; High (tick): the 2018–2023 rate persists; Very High: the 1991–2023 census-interval trend continues; instead of the 2018–2023 rate fading to the long-run rate with a 10-year half-life. Replacement half-life (5–15 yr): 5 / 15 years instead of 10. Soil order (Raw–Organic): the soil carbon loss of the lowest (Raw) / highest (Organic) soil order on every new footprint instead of the area-weighted mean over the soil orders of the Auckland land zoned for urbanisation. Single case study (lowest–highest): the materials factor of the lowest / highest single case study of each typology instead of the pooled typology factor. Module D credit, booked at construction (not netted): the Module D credit (benefits beyond the system boundary, EN 15978) of the 2026–2050 cohorts at 2025 factors (the largest credit), booked in the construction year and subtracted; carbon only; not converted to LoE, because a consistent LoE would need Module D in the historical sector base as well. Frozen technology (2025 factors held): every factor held at 2025 instead of A1–A3 on the item paths of Horup et al. (2025) and A4–A5 falling 1% per year. Production decarbonisation: no-policy backgrounds (Horup MAX): A1-A3 of construction and in-window events x [MAX(y)/MAX(2025)] / [AVG(y)/AVG(2025)] of the 9 backgrounds (Horup et al. 2025, Table S3) from 2027: the no-climate-policy end of L10; carbon only. Carbon factors (jackknife): the lowest / highest pooled materials factor when each case study is left out in turn, instead of the pooled factor (a spread, not a confidence interval). NZ-made electricity-intensive items held at 2025 factors: items made in New Zealand with electricity-intensive production held at 2025 instead of following their Horup et al. (2025) path. A4–A5 decarbonisation (own path–held at 2025): A4–A5 on each item's own Horup et al. (2025) path / held at 2025 instead of the generic 1% per year decline (Resch et al. 2021). Soil carbon loss on all floor area, incl. replacement: soil carbon loss also on replacement floor area instead of none on rebuilt footprints. Proxy-mapped items held at 2025 factors: items mapped to a proxy material held at 2025 instead of following the proxy's path.

- Files: `paper_extended/ED8_one_at_a_time.png`
- Data: `data/sensitivity/reference_carbon.csv`, `data/sensitivity/tl_sensitivity.csv`
- This run: (a) Reference 25,503 kt. One at a time: not additive, not a joint interval. "No effect": every case within 0.01% of the Reference. Not shown: the superseded-setting rows (completion rate 0.95, completion lag 0 months and the never-absorbed overbuild) and the overbuild gap measured against the 2026 requirement (+0.0028%); no census under-construction correction (+0.0000%); maintenance event timing L / n (-0.6961%) (in the data file). ### ED9_sobol

**ED9 Sobol indices of the Reference: embodied carbon and floor area 2026-2050** — First-order and total-effect Sobol indices of the Reference cumulative embodied carbon and floor area 2026-2050 for the sampled inputs (population rank, dwelling-size multiplier, completion rate and the case-study carbon-factor bootstrap), from the full-profile Monte Carlo; bars are the estimates, whiskers their bootstrap intervals.

- Files: `paper_extended/ED9_sobol.png`
- Data: `data/montecarlo/sobol_REF.csv`
- This run: Reference, cumulative 2026–2050; Saltelli / Jansen estimators (scipy.stats.sobol_indices); 95% intervals by bootstrap of the Sobol samples; full profile only. Population and household size are one grouped input: both are drawn from one standard-normal score z (perfectly dependent), so their indices are grouped Sobol indices (Jacques, Lavergne & Devictor 2006).

## Supplementary figures (supplementary/)

### SF1_households

**SF1 Households: the published and census-benchmarked series, and household size against population growth**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF1_households.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D02_households.json`, `data/figure_source/D04_household_formation.json`
- This run: a: projection from the 2023 census point; 2019–23 Stats NZ estimates scaled to the 2023 census (×0.824); 2024–2025: households = population / household size (model), on the projection line. The band: the 5th / 95th population percentile paths with the Stats NZ Low A / High A household size (households computed per path). b: between censuses households are consent-derived, so the relationship is partly mechanical (housing supply meets migration); 2024-25 are the model household-size path (ERP / S), not observations.

### SF2_completion_lag

**SF2 Annual floor area by demand group: 17-month and like-for-like zero completion lag**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF2_completion_lag.png`
- Data: `data/diagnostics/lag_comparison_annual.csv`, `data/diagnostics/lag_comparison_summary.json`
- This run: All runs use identical source files and demographic paths. The like-for-like zero-lag run holds the forward net replacement at the 17-month calibration (2018-2023 rate 0.173%/yr), so it differs from the 17-month run only in the timing of building. The recalibrated zero-lag run (grey, context) re-estimates net replacement from the census counts with zero-lag timing (0.301%/yr with the census under-construction correction); its higher net replacement in panel c is that recalibration, not the timing of building. Cumulative net replacement 2026-2050: 9.02 Mm² (zero lag, held), 9.29 Mm² (17 months), 15.24 Mm² (zero lag, recalibrated). Zero lag treats a rolling 12-month consent estimate as the 2026 build proxy; the 17-month run uses complete observed consent cohorts for 2026 and 2027.

### SF3_vacancy_definition

**SF3 Vacancy definition: unconsented additions each definition requires**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF3_vacancy_definition.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D06_vacancy_definition.json`
- This run: The unconsented additions each vacancy definition requires to close the stock identity (BRANZ demolition rate); counting residents-away dwellings as vacant requires implausibly many.

### SF4_overbuild_absorption

**SF4 The starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild: absorption in the Reference and its timing sensitivity**

- Files: `supplementary/calibration/SF4_overbuild_absorption.png`
- Data: `data/baseline/overbuild_absorption_log.csv`, `data/baseline/sensitivity_annual_carbon.csv`
- This run: The surplus still vacant U(t) starts with the starting surplus of 18,966 dwellings (the 2024–2025 building beyond the stock identity, carried into 2026), to which the 2026 overbuild adds; both are paid back along the same logistic by 2035. Theory fixes the direction (reversion to the equilibrium vacancy), not the speed; 2035 is the common RECC window; speed bracketed.

### SF5_hindcast

**SF5 Rolling-origin hindcast of dwellings built and the 2027 out-of-sample check**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF5_hindcast.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D14_hindcast.json`, `data/baseline/validation.json`
- This run: Rolling-origin hindcast of dwellings built (cumulative), each origin projected with the information available then; errors at the end of each window, vacancy on the consistent definition. The four replacement variants use only the census intervals ending at or before the origin: Low the long-run dwelling-count rate, Reference the last intercensal rate fading to it (10-year half-life), High the last rate held, Very High the weighted linear trend of the interval rates (3, 4 and 5 intervals at the 2006, 2013 and 2018 origins). d: building of the first year the run without 2026 data models, observed in the pipeline (consents lagged), against that run.

### SF6_reality_checks

**SF6 Reality checks: the projection against the 1991-2025 range**

- Files: `supplementary/validation/SF6_reality_checks.png`
- Data: `data/figure_source/D15_reality_checks.json`, `data/baseline/annual.csv`, `data/baseline/variants_annual.csv`
- This run: Projection 2026–2050 against the 1991–2025 range (grey band); b: implied net removals = net replacement rate × stock; h: consented floor area, in scope; a: in scope and retirement villages; the exceedances are tabulated in outputs/reports/reality_checks.md. b: Low and High hold a constant rate (Low: the 1991–2023 long-run rate; High: the 2018–2023 rate); removals rise because the stock grows. The Reference rate fades from the 2018–2023 rate to the long-run rate (half-life 10 yr); Very High continues the census trend. History lines: straight segments between annual values (not smoothed; largest difference from the source data 0); b: census-interval rates, constant within each interval. Handover: the 2027 → 2028 step of the Reference floor area (2027 observed, 2028 the first model year) is −8.2%, against year-to-year changes of −39.8% to +27.8% (median +3.0%) in consented floor area, 1992–2025.

### SF13_conditional_tl

**SF13 When does TL stay within AR? By population quintile and the population threshold**

- Files: `supplementary/montecarlo/SF13_conditional_tl.png`

- This run: P(within AR) = 0.609 (Wilson 0.596-0.623); (b) threshold 6.69 M (95% CI 6.69-6.70 M; Firth penalised likelihood (MLE does not exist), 2000 resamples). With L1 at TL from the lowest observed census headship of each age group (or propensity B where lower; 4.0% fewer) TL is 5,963 kt, LoE AR 1.35, P(LoE AR ≤ 1) = 0.04% over the draws (sensitivity row).
